text: The Constitution of Nepal was promulgated on 20 September 2015 by the second Constituent Assembly.
Article 4 declares Nepal an independent, indivisible, sovereign, secular, inclusive, democratic, socialism-oriented federal democratic republican state.
Article 7 makes the Nepali language in the Devanagari script the official language of Nepal.
Article 16 guarantees every person the right to live with dignity, and no law may provide for the death penalty.
Article 17 guarantees freedom of opinion and expression, freedom to assemble peaceably, and freedom to form political parties.
Article 18 states that all citizens are equal before the law and prohibits discrimination on grounds such as caste, sex, religion, or language.
Article 27 gives every citizen the right to demand and receive information on any matter of their own or of public interest.
Article 30 gives every citizen the right to live in a clean and healthy environment, with compensation for victims of pollution.
Article 31 gives every citizen the right of access to basic education, and free and compulsory education up to the basic level.
Article 35 gives every citizen the right to free basic health services from the State and to emergency health services.
Article 39 protects the rights of the child, including the right to a name, education, health care, and protection from child labour.
Article 56 sets out three levels of the State: the federation, the provinces, and the local level.
Nepal is divided into seven provinces, each with its own provincial assembly and government.
The local level consists of 753 units: metropolitan cities, sub-metropolitan cities, municipalities, and rural municipalities.
Article 61 makes the President the head of state, who promotes national unity and safeguards the Constitution.
Article 76 provides that the President appoints as Prime Minister the leader of the parliamentary party commanding a majority in the House of Representatives.
Article 84 sets the House of Representatives at 275 members: 165 elected by first-past-the-post and 110 by proportional representation.
Article 86 makes the National Assembly a permanent house of 59 members, one third of whom retire every two years.
Article 128 establishes the Supreme Court as the highest court, with final authority to interpret the Constitution and the law.
Article 245 establishes the Election Commission, which conducts and supervises elections at every level.
